author: A. Stein
asr_identification: Kua-chou-ch'êng, the ruined walled town S of An-hsi (Guazhou county town), Gansu
evidence: Central position in the oasis and local tradition; from it 8 miles due N in a straight line to where the Hami road crosses the Su-lo Ho, 10 miles to an old river bed: the Life's 50 li at 5 li to the mile. The walls (c. ½ × ⅓ mile) held a Qing ya-men; no Tang finds are cited.
quote: which in view of its central position and surviving local tradition may safely be assumed to mark the approximate site of the Kua-chou of T'ang times
note: differs from the recent consensus (Suoyang cheng, 01.04.x1 note); Stein's site is about 30 km W of Suoyang cheng

author: A. Stein
asr_identification: the Su-lo Ho (Shule river, Bulungir), after V. de Saint-Martin
evidence: The road north from Kua-chou-ch'êng meets the Su-lo Ho after 8 miles (an old bed 2 miles further N).
quote: By the river Hu-lu no other but the Su-lo Ho can be meant
note: agrees with the Shule; the channel and crossing point are disputed

author: A. Stein
asr_identification: not located; somewhere on the Su-lo N of Kua-chou, moved there not long before 629
evidence: He cannot place the pass of 629; the Han pass lay far W of Dunhuang, and in 610 the pass was at Chin-ch'ang, so it had moved since.
quote: As to the exact position of the Yi-mên Barrier, as located at the time of Hsüan-tsang's departure, I am unable to state anything definite

author: A. Stein
asr_identification: Pei-tan-tzů (Baidunzi), the first stage from An-hsi on the Hami road, with its spring
evidence: About 16 miles on the map from the old Su-lo bed to Pei-tan-tzů, against the Life's 80 li from the crossing; the beacon had water below it, as the stage has a spring.
quote: the first signal-tower clearly points to the present Pei-tan-tzů, the first stage from An-hsi
note: Stein's identification rests on 5 li to the mile and the spring

author: A. Stein
asr_identification: Ma-lien-ching-tzů (Malianjing), the fourth stage, with wells 6–8 feet deep
evidence: Five beacons 100 li apart from the 80-li first: 480 li from the river to the fifth = 96 miles by cyclometer to Hsing-hsing-hsia, the fifth stage; so the fourth is Ma-lien-ching-tzů. The Life's one night from the first to the fourth beacon is a lacuna: two marches are missing.
quote: from Ma-lien-ching-tzů, i.e, the fourth signal-tower

author: A. Stein
asr_identification: the Life omits two marches between the first and fourth beacons
evidence: The Life has Xuanzang reach the fourth beacon the night after leaving the first, against its own 100 li between beacons.
quote: We are thus obliged to assume that Hsuan-tsang in reality had to cover four marches from the river before reaching the fourth tower
note: a reading of the text, not site evidence

author: A. Stein
name_in_asr: Yeh-ma-ch'üan, 'The Spring of the Wild Horses'
asr_identification: a water stage on Roborovsky's Dunhuang–Hami route, about 30 miles WNW of Ma-lien-ching-tzů
evidence: He turned east to regain the fourth beacon, so the spring lay W of the road; the Russian map shows a water stage on the Dunhuang–Hami track about that far WNW of Ma-lien-ching-tzů. Not visited.
quote: Thus the existence, in the past or present, of a spring approximately in the position indicated for the Yeh-ma-ch'üan which Hsüan-tsang vainly sought for, becomes very probable

author: A. Stein
asr_identification: the ground beyond Hsing-hsing-hsia (the fifth beacon): Sha-ch'üan-tzu, K'u-shui and the Yen-tun depression
evidence: The 480 li from the river to the fifth beacon match 96 cyclometer miles to Hsing-hsing-hsia; beyond it the ground changes for the worse (2,000 ft descent, brackish water, the 35-mile waterless march K'u-shui–Yen-tun).
quote: The 480 li reckoned from the Su-lo Ho to the fifth signal-tower are in remarkably exact agreement with 96 miles marching distance recorded by cyclometer
note: the Moheyan as the Hsing-hsing-hsia–Chang-liu-shui stretch

author: A. Stein
name_in_asr: pasture and water in a pool
asr_identification: near Chang-liu-shui (Changliushui), the first spring and verdure on the Hami side
evidence: Five marches, 106 miles, on the road from Ma-lien-ching-tzů to Chang-liu-shui, against four nights and five days without water; his line ran roughly parallel to the road and missed its wells.
quote: to Chang-liu-shui, the first place with spring water and verdure on the Hami side, the total marching distance amounting to 106 miles

author: A. Stein
evidence: Two marches, some 35 miles, from Chang-liu-shui to Hami town, as the Life's two days from the pool.
quote: the two more days which it makes Hsüan-tsang spend en route before reaching Hami correspond exactly to the two marches now reckoned from Chang-liu-shui to Hami town

author: A. Stein
asr_identification: not where it was in 610 (at Chin-ch'ang, a sub-prefecture of Kua-chou E of An-hsi); position in 629 unknown
evidence: The Sui annals put the pass at Chin-ch'ang in 610; the pass of 629 lay on the river 50 li N of Kua-chou; he doubts any remains would survive by a shifting river.
quote: distinctly places this frontier station at the town of … was not where Hstian-tsang found it twenty years later
note: the Jinchang link is the base of the later Shuangta view

author: A. Stein
asr_identification: a tower of recent origin W of An-hsi (Map 81 c. 3)
evidence: In 1907 Surveyor Ram Singh reported the large towers sighted W of An-hsi to be of recent origin; Stein confirms this for Lei-tun-tzu, which Ram Singh visited; in 1914 he traced the Han wall with its badly decayed towers to within a couple of miles of it.
quote: were  reported  by’ Surveyor … to  he  of  recent  origin … report  was  correct  as  regards  the  tower … which  he  actually  visited
note: the Leidunzi beacon (40°29.787′ N, 95°32.627′ E), the older placing of the Xinjing post; agrees with Huang Yinzhou et al. 2024 that it is late

author: A. Stein
name_in_asr: large conspicuous tower at the E end of the limes W of An-hsi
asr_identification: a new-looking tower, perhaps on an old core; unnamed
evidence: 1914: from T. xxxvii. k the Han agger turned due E towards a large conspicuous tower, reached after a mile, new in appearance but perhaps built round an old core; beyond it the line was lost in reeds and scrub near the An-hsi cultivation.
quote: turned  due  east  in  the  direction  of  a  large  conspicuous  tower … found  to  be  new  in  appearance,  but  might  well have  been  built  round  an  old  one  serving  as  its  core
note: unnamed; may be Lei-tun-tzu (Serindia iii p. 1093 n. 2 says the 1914 tracing stopped a couple of miles short of it), not established
